transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I think I got in over my head. I took on this historical society fundraiser like I could run the whole thing myself—started quilt designs, called volunteers, made schedules, and promised deadlines that, looking back, I really couldn’t meet.
During the time you took all this on, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or more energized than normal?

Yes. At first I felt really energized, almost glowing, like every idea I had was a good one. I felt very sure of myself. But if someone questioned me or slowed me down, I’d get snappish, like they were getting in my way.
During that energized period, did you ever hear or see things other people couldn’t, or believe something that others said wasn’t true?

I didn’t hear or see things, no. But I did believe, very strongly, that my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map. Like I had finally found the thing only I could do, and I could make it happen.
During that energized period, were you hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I wasn’t taken to a hospital or admitted anywhere for it, if that’s what you mean. It was more that people around me got concerned.
During that energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your day-to-day functioning?

Yes, it did. I stopped keeping up with things I’d promised to do, especially with the historical society, and then I couldn’t face the people who were waiting on me. My husband had to step in and handle the household routines and deal with them for me. It caused real problems.
About how many days did that unusually energized, confident, and irritable period last?
It lasted a long time—about five months, I’d say. That whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project went on for months before everything really fell apart.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?

Yes. Lately I’ve lost interest in things I used to really enjoy. I used to love going out and checking my garden, and working on my quilt entries, but now I’ll just look at the fabric or the seed catalogs and… I don’t feel much of anything.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a prolonged distinct period of abnormally elevated/expansive and irritable mood with increased energy, inflated self-confidence/grandiose ideas, excessive goal-directed activity, and clear functional impairment lasting about five months. This is sufficient for a manic episode. She also reports a depressive period with loss of interest, supporting a bipolar spectrum illness. No substance/medical cause or psychotic disorder was established in the interview.
